outcomeTags.tag: `required`: the expected outcome follows from the cited clauses and can fail an implementation. `labChoice`: the laboratory's outcome where the text leaves it open; a differing implementation is reported and does not fail.
outcomeTags.classTag: On a refusal, the verdict is compared under `tag`; the refusal class is compared only when `classTag` is `required` (the default). The laboratory refusal classes are `format`, `structure`, `integrity`, `signature`, `decode`, `root-pk-mismatch` and `delegation-invalid`; ENV names `integrity`, `signature` and `decode` refusals, and KEYS §2.7 names the last two. `detail` is the laboratory's label and is never compared for an implementation.

generator.deterministic: Fixed public test roots, frozen random values and RFC 6979 low-S ES256 nonces; `node generate.mjs --check` reproduces both files byte for byte.

decisions.text: Every value is computed under the laboratory deployment profile `tpnil-sdx-lab:v1` (fixtures/sdx/v1/deployment-profile.json). `proto` and the outer protected-header `proto` carry its format identifier `tpnil-sdx-lab:v1`. The signing key identifier is derived under [2, `sdx sign`] and the recipient identifiers under [2, `sdx encrypt`], with key ID `account/<accountId>/runtime/<runtimeId>/action/<actionId>` and, per field, `/field/<fieldName>` appended; the level-3 keyword `action` is the profile's reading R1. Basis: ENV §2, §2.1, §8.5, §8.6; KEYS §1.3.1, §1.6.1, §1.8.

Each case is a request of the laboratory driver contract (programs/proposals/sdx-data-sharing/0.1.0/driver-contract.md) and its expected result. A `read` case expects a projection: the tier reached, the verdict, the refusal class, `aid`, the header values, one entry per declared field in declared order with its state (`value`, `unset` or `redacted`) and the verifying signature's `kid` and shape. A `write` case expects either a writer refusal or an envelope; for an envelope the laboratory publishes its own bytes and the checks of `checkWrite` in src/sdx/env.mjs, and the read cases marked `fromWrite` are rerun on the writer's envelope.

Every write case carries `random`: per JWE the content-encryption key, the IV, one ephemeral private key per identity recipient in recipient order, and for a convergent slot the key-wrap IV. Given them, a writer's wrapped keys and IVs are deterministic, and `checkWrite` compares them byte for byte (checks marked `random`). Ciphertexts are not compared: they depend on the LZMA encoder (decision lzma-container) and on the ES256 nonce, which SDX does not fix. They are judged by decryption.

The ENV §9 compression step writes the .lzma "alone" container: a 13-byte header (properties byte, 4-byte little-endian dictionary size, 8-byte little-endian uncompressed size, here the actual size) followed by the raw stream with no end-of-stream marker. The laboratory writer is LZMA-JS 2.3.2 in mode 9 with its `disableEndMark` switch (lc 3, lp 0, pb 2, a 32 MiB dictionary). `checkWrite` requires the stream to carry no end-of-stream marker (`required`, ENV §9) and the header to carry the size (`labChoice`); readers accept a stream that carries the marker (`labChoice`). Source findings: ENV §9 and §13 name LZMA, level 9 and a disabled end marker but no container; and encoders differ at "level 9" (LZMA-JS writes a 32 MiB dictionary, liblzma 64 MiB), so the compressed bytes are encoder-specific and readers compare the decompressed bytes. The Node oracle's own decoder (src/sdx/lzma.mjs) detects the marker; Python's lzma module decodes both forms and cannot tell them apart. Basis: ENV §9, §13 step 4.

A private field's plaintext is the deterministic encoding of the shortest array that holds every present element of [value, filename?, mediaType?, meta?], with an absent element before the last present one written as null. Readers accept an array of 1 to 4 elements and treat null as absent. Source finding: ENV §9 writes the tuple with optional elements and ENV §3 encodes an absent array element as null, so the text does not fix whether trailing absent elements are written. Basis: ENV §3 (absent-value table), §9, §13 step 4, §14 step 10.

The outer protected header holds exactly {enc, proto, aid}, plus iter and salt on a convergent record, and each identity recipient carries its own ephemeral key in its header {alg, kid, epk}. A per-field JWE's protected header is {enc}, plus iter and salt when the field declares `cv`. `checkWrite` requires both (`required`). Readers also open a JWE whose single recipient's `epk` sits in the protected header (`labChoice`), which is what a stock JOSE library writes for one recipient (jose 6.2.17 GeneralEncrypt does). Basis: ENV §5.2, §9, §11, §13 steps 4 and 10.

A per-field JWE lists the convergent slot (when `cv`), then the writer self-recipient (unless writer-blind), then the external recipients in request order; the self-recipient comes before any external one (`required`). The outer wrap lists the convergent slot, then the writer self-recipient, then the audit recipients; the outer position of the self-recipient is the laboratory's choice (`labChoice`), and its presence is required. Basis: ENV §5.2, §9 (notes on the ordering), §13 steps 4 and 10.

A convergent field's A256GCMKW slot is keyed by HMAC-SHA-256(key = s2, message = s1) of the field plaintext, and the outer convergent slot by the record-level s1 of the audit-layer bytes. The convergent slot carries no `kid`. `salt` is the base64url of the SHA-256 (`labChoice`; ENV §6.1 rule 6 leaves its shape open). A record is convergent when any private descriptor declares `cv`, set or unset (ENV §13 step 9). Source finding: ENV §9 says the per-field key is HMAC(s2, s1) "exactly as the record-level derivation is over the audit layer's", while ENV §5.2, §12 and §13 step 10 key the outer convergent slot with s1 itself; the laboratory reads "exactly as" as the same calculateSecrets and follows §5.2 and §13 for the key. Basis: ENV §4, §5.2, §6.1, §9, §12, §13.

The ENV §4 known-answer cases pin calculateSecrets with iterations 200000: the HMAC key is s2 and the message s1. Each case also records, as an oracle note, the value the reversed order gives, which a conforming implementation never produces. An iteration count below 200000 is refused. The cases use the driver contract's `secrets` hook; an implementation that exposes no such hook is BLOCKED on them and is still checked through R4's convergent slots. Basis: ENV §4.

A reader computes one candidate key per layer from the protected-header `aid` (outer) or the header `aid` (fields): its own child under the record's recipient key identifier, with counterparty its own root (`as: writer`) or the writer's P-256 root (`as: reader`). It attempts only a slot whose `kid` is that key's hex. With no outer slot it stays at the Nothing tier, which is not a refusal. Basis: ENV §5.3, §8.6, §12, §14 step 4.

A reader whose field key's hex is not among a private slot's identity identifiers declines it: the field is `redacted` and the decode continues. Before honouring the decline it validates everything the decryption step would (canonical base64url, IV and tag lengths, `enc`, the effective header as a disjoint union, and per recipient the identifier point, the ephemeral key and the wrapped-key length); each failure is an integrity refusal. A JWE with no recipient list is refused, never redacted. A reader that is a recipient takes the ordinary route, where a malformed later slot does not matter. An unset field never reaches the resolver. Basis: ENV §7.1, §9.1 rules 2 and 3, §12, §14 step 10, §15.

A refused record is reported with a laboratory class: `format` (not a record of a configured profile, ENV §2, §3, §14 steps 1-2), `structure` (the ENV §6-§8.1 rules that name no class), `integrity`, `signature` and `decode` (named by ENV §5.3, §8.3, §9.1, §14, §15, §17.5), and `root-pk-mismatch` and `delegation-invalid` (KEYS §2.7). The class is compared only where the text names it (`classTag` `required`); elsewhere the verdict alone is compared. A refused projection carries no field.

A writer refuses, before any encryption: a writer-blind field without an external recipient, an unset private field placed off the envelope or carrying metadata, a field name repeated across sensitivities (after NFC normalisation), `cv` on a public or audit field, `cv` other than `true`, a writer-blind field with `cv`, and a field name containing `/` or outside 1 to 256 bytes. The harness compares that the writer refused; the `detail` labels are the laboratory's. Basis: ENV §6.1, §7.1, §9, §9.1 rules 1 and 5, §13 step 4; KEYS §1.6.2.

Field names are NFC-normalised before they enter the header and the key path; a request that gives a decomposed name produces a descriptor and a key in the composed form. Basis: ENV §6.1; KEYS §1.6.2.

No case exercises the ENV §15 marker-refusal rules 5, 6, 8 and 9. Source finding: ENV §15 leaves the representation of the redacted, unavailable and erased markers to each implementation, and those rules turn on that representation, so no interoperable vector can state an input that resembles "a marker". The projection reports markers as field states, which implementations map from their own representation. Basis: ENV §15.

Every case places fields in-record (`pl` "ch"). Externalised values (ENV §10 and the field-placement section) wait for SDX's unpublished `placement` suite; the laboratory reader has no store and no overlay resolver, and the projection states `unavailable` and `erased` are reserved for that suite. The placement rules that need no store are covered: the unset marker on an `ov` descriptor and an unset private field placed `ov`. Basis: ENV §7 rule 3, §7.1, §10; BASE §6 item 4.

Account and runtime identifiers are base58 (Bitcoin alphabet) of 16 bytes followed by the first 4 bytes of their SHA-256d, with no version byte; the bytes are SHA-256 of a published label. Record identifiers are ULIDs whose time is the record's `tm`. Source finding: KEYS §1.6.2 names base58check for 128-bit identifiers without fixing a version byte or the checksum. Identifiers are opaque to every derivation, so the choice changes no rule. Basis: KEYS §1.6.2, §1.6.3.

The Node oracle bounds CBOR nesting at 64, CBOR input at 16 MiB and LZMA output at 16 MiB. ENV §17.6 requires bounds and fixes no values, so a refusal caused by one of them when reading an implementation's output is ERROR, never FAIL.

oracles.generatorWitness: jose 6.2.17 opens every JWE of every known-answer record through every recipient (ECDH-ES+A256KW and A256GCMKW) and verifies every known-answer ES256 signature; the generator builds JWEs on @noble primitives from the frozen values.

node.covers: Every step of every case: CBOR, the ENV §14 decode flow, the JOSE steps by hand on node:crypto (ECDH, Concat KDF, AES key wrap, AES-GCM, A256GCMKW), ES256 on both candidate shapes, KEYS §1.8.2 derivation, its own LZMA decoder (which also detects an end-of-stream marker) and ENV §4 PBKDF2.
node.agreement: The generator declares each expected outcome from the case's construction; the checker reproduces every one, including the laboratory refusal detail, or generation stops.

python.covers: Every step of every case: CBOR, the decode flow, the JOSE steps by hand (its AES-256, GCM and key unwrap are pure Python in test/sdx_ec.py), ES256 on both candidate shapes, KEYS §1.8.2 derivation, LZMA through the standard library's lzma module (FORMAT_ALONE; it cannot tell whether an end-of-stream marker was written, which only the Node oracle checks) and ENV §4 PBKDF2.

Known-answer record R1: public, audit and private fields, set and unset, two audit recipients and per-field recipient lists: read by the writer, holding only its root. Holding only its root, the writer reaches every tier through its self-recipient slots (ENV §5.2, §12 self-replication).

Known-answer record R1: public, audit and private fields, set and unset, two audit recipients and per-field recipient lists: read by reader A. A is on the outer wrap and on both private fields, so it reads everything.

Known-answer record R1: public, audit and private fields, set and unset, two audit recipients and per-field recipient lists: read by reader B. B is on the outer wrap and on `site` only: `kwh` is redacted and the decode continues (ENV §9.1 rule 2, §15 rule 3).

Known-answer record R1: public, audit and private fields, set and unset, two audit recipients and per-field recipient lists: read by outsider O. O holds no slot: the Nothing tier, with `proto`, the public slots and `aid` from the protected header (ENV §12, §14 step 4).
Known-answer record R2: one audit field and no external recipient; the outer wrap carries the writer self-recipient alone

Known-answer record R2: one audit field and no external recipient; the outer wrap carries the writer self-recipient alone: read by the writer, holding only its root. The self-recipient is the one access path (ENV §5.2).

Known-answer record R2: one audit field and no external recipient; the outer wrap carries the writer self-recipient alone: read by reader A. A is not addressed and stays at the Nothing tier; the record has no public field.
Known-answer record R3: a writer-blind private field whose only recipient is A

Known-answer record R3: a writer-blind private field whose only recipient is A: read by the writer, holding only its root. The writer keeps the audit tier and every other field, and its resolver declines the blind field, which surfaces as redacted (ENV §9.1 rule 2, §12).
Known-answer record R3: a writer-blind private field whose only recipient is A: read by reader A. A reads the blind field through its own slot.
Known-answer record R4: a convergent private field; the outer protected header carries iter and salt, and both layers carry an A256GCMKW slot

Known-answer record R4: a convergent private field; the outer protected header carries iter and salt, and both layers carry an A256GCMKW slot: read by the writer, holding only its root. The identity slots open it; the convergent slots are not offered to the key resolver (ENV §5.2, §9.1 rule 2(a)).

Known-answer record R4: a convergent private field; the outer protected header carries iter and salt, and both layers carry an A256GCMKW slot: read by reader A. A reads the convergent field through its identity slot.

Known-answer record R5: a field name given in decomposed form (stored and derived in NFC), the full private tuple, a null audit value and a negative integer: read by reader A. A recovers value, filename, media type and meta from the tuple.

Known-answer record R5: a field name given in decomposed form (stored and derived in NFC), the full private tuple, a null audit value and a negative integer: read by reader B. B is not addressed: the Nothing tier, with no public field.
